governanceNotes: Postoperative atrial fibrillation is documented in roughly 23% of isolated-CABG patients without prior AF (both 2025 cohorts), but the Kuroda CREDO-Kyoto analysis found no excess adjusted all-cause mortality at 5 years with numerically higher stroke and heart failure, so long-term clinical significance beyond the perioperative window is actively debated and must be individually documented rather than presumed.

The cognitive-disorder incidence figures (80-90% at discharge, 42% at 5 years) are review-cited literature values from Román 2002, not a single cohort; POCD studies are sensitive to test-battery and control-group choices (Funder 2009), and delirium-trajectory data (Saczynski 2012) show substantial individual recovery - persistence beyond the typical recovery window is the claim-relevant question for a qualified professional.

nexusClaim.etiologicalTrigger: This DIRECT_CAUSATION classification is about the proposed treatment-mediated theory, not a population-level statement that coronary artery disease causes arrhythmia: coronary bypass surgery residuals (the post-CABG state) -> postoperative atrial fibrillation arising from the surgery itself, if documented -> claimed cardiac arrhythmia identity; the exposure is the surgery, not the underlying atherosclerosis, and agent-specific documentation (operation date, arrhythmia onset, persistence) is required. Postoperative atrial fibrillation is recognized as a common complication of isolated CABG in patients with no prior AF.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A post-surgical atrial substrate pathway is documented: pericardial inflammation, autonomic surge, atrial stretch from fluid shifts, and ischemia-reperfusion after cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamping produce the transient atrial electrical substrate of postoperative atrial fibrillation, classically in the first postoperative week; cohort data show POAF in roughly 23% of isolated-CABG patients with no prior AF, with prolonged cross-clamp time, age, and reduced GFR as predictors. The mechanism is surgical, so the classification is the treatment-mediated theory only.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The treatment-mediated theory is classified DIRECT_CAUSATION per the repository's iatrogenic convention because the arrhythmia arises as a direct complication of the surgery itself, not as an association requiring population-level inference; whether the individual veteran's documented arrhythmia satisfies the theory is a determination for a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: operative report establishing the CABG date and cardiopulmonary-bypass/cross-clamp details; rhythm documentation (ECG/monitor) of the arrhythmia with onset relative to surgery; persistence or recurrence pattern after discharge; pre-operative rhythm history excluding prior atrial fibrillation; exclusion of hyperthyroidism, valvular disease, alcohol, and pulmonary causes; a medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Pre-existing paroxysmal atrial fibrillation unmasked by perioperative monitoring
Underlying valvular or congenital heart disease
Hyperthyroidism, alcohol use, pulmonary embolism, or pneumonia
Atherosclerotic atrial ischemia independent of the surgery

nexusClaim.etiologicalTrigger: This DIRECT_CAUSATION classification is about the proposed treatment-mediated theory, not a population-level statement that coronary artery disease causes dementia: coronary bypass surgery residuals (the post-CABG state) -> postoperative cognitive dysfunction/neurocognitive decline arising from the surgery itself, if documented -> claimed cognitive disorder identity; the exposure is the surgery, not the underlying atherosclerosis, and documentation of the cognitive trajectory across the operation is required.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A post-surgical neurocognitive-injury pathway is documented: microemboli from cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic manipulation, cerebral hypoperfusion, systemic inflammatory response, and perioperative delirium produce measurable cognitive dysfunction after CABG; longitudinal data show lower MMSE trajectories through one year in delirium patients with 40% not returned to baseline at six months, and reviews record measurable dysfunction in 80-90% at hospital discharge with a 42% five-year incidence, with long-term consequences for quality of life and survival. The mechanism is surgical, so the classification is the treatment-mediated theory only.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The treatment-mediated theory is classified DIRECT_CAUSATION per the repository's iatrogenic convention because the cognitive injury arises as a direct consequence of the surgery itself, not as an association requiring population-level inference; whether the individual veteran's documented deficits satisfy the theory, and whether they persist beyond the typical recovery window, is a determination for a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: operative report establishing the CABG date, bypass strategy (on/off-pump), and complications; pre-operative and post-operative cognitive testing or documentation showing decline with chronology; delirium documentation during the index admission where available; persistence pattern (recovery versus sustained deficit) over follow-up; exclusion of stroke, hypoxia, medication effects, depression-related pseudodementia, and pre-existing neurodegenerative disease; a medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Intraoperative stroke or documented hypoxic injury (a distinct mechanism requiring separate documentation)
Pre-existing mild cognitive impairment or neurodegenerative disease progressing independently
Post-operative depression presenting as cognitive complaints (pseudodementia)
Medication effects (benzodiazepines, opioids, anticholinergics) during recovery
Vascular cognitive impairment from the underlying atherosclerotic disease itself rather than the surgery
